1. We have a property-test framework
2. The Block + Stmt construction work (vez6.3.9) lands so the fuzzer can cover that surface area too.

title: lower_quotes: fine-grained change tracking for in-place subtree reuse
description:
When a file DOES contain a quote expression, lower_quotes still walks every Stmt/Expr in the file and reallocates Stmt/Expr nodes for every container — even subtrees that contain no Quote.

The fast-path in lower_quotes already eliminates the cost for files with NO quotes. This ticket is the next-level optimization: for files WITH quotes, recursively decide per-subtree whether to allocate new nodes.

Implementation sketch:
- Change lower_expr to return {expr: Expr, changed: bool}
- Each container arm checks if any child's changed=true; only allocates a fresh Binary/Call/etc node when at least one child changed
- Same for lower_stmt / lower_stmt_list / etc

This pattern needs a sister implementation in comptime/rewrite.av and desugar.av (same walker shape, same allocation cost). Coordinated with the generic-AST-visitor ticket (93k3) — likely best implemented once the visitor abstraction lands.

Estimated win: maybe 50% allocation reduction for files with quotes (most subtrees contain no quote). Marginal in absolute terms (quote files are rare). Not blocking.

title: bd: parent-child relationship doesn't gate 'bd ready' even though dep error says it does
description:
bd refuses to add an explicit `dep add child parent` with the message 'Children inherit dependency on parent completion via hierarchy. Adding an explicit dependency would create a deadlock.'

But `bd ready` shows children as ready even when their parent is open. The two behaviors disagree: bd is claiming the parent-child IS a dep, but treating it as if it isn't.

Repro:
  bd create --title=parent --type=epic
  bd create --title=child --parent=<parent-id>
  bd ready
  # → child shows as ready, even though parent is still open

Expected: either parent-child gates ready (consistent with dep_add error), or bd allows the explicit dep to be added.

Hit while wiring blocking deps for cleanup sub-tickets — wanted cleanup to only show ready after parent phase is done. Currently impossible: bd refuses the explicit dep, but the implicit parent-child doesn't gate ready.

Workaround: ignore the early cleanup-in-ready entries during phase work. Annoying but not blocking.

title: features/eval Runtime: hashmap-backed lookup_function (also helps bs2 eval REPL)
description:
features/eval/mod.av's `lookup_function` is an O(N) linear scan over `runtime.functions`. Called from:

- eval_expr → Ident lookup_function (if Ident is a fn name)
- eval_call → lookup_function (re-resolves callee_value's fn name)
- eval_expr → QualifiedIdent lookup_function

Per call, that's potentially 2× O(N) lookups. For the comptime use case post vez6.11 (std-cli rewrite), N grows into 50-100 comptime fns, and call sites grow into hundreds. The current setup spends measurable time in linear scans.

## Approach

Add a name→index hashmap to Runtime, populated alongside `functions`:

  type Runtime = {
      bindings: List<Binding>,
      functions: List<FunctionDef>,
      function_index: ptr,    // NEW: string → int index in functions
      depth: int,
      features: Registry,
  }

`define_function` updates both `functions` and `function_index`. `lookup_function` becomes:

  if avra_map_has_cstr(rt.function_index, name) == 0 { return not-found }
  rt.functions[avra_map_get_cstr(rt.function_index, name)]

## Estimated impact

For programs with N=20 fns, M=500 calls: 20×500×2 = 20k linear-scan compare ops eliminated. ~5% of comptime pass time.

For larger programs (N=100, M=5000): much bigger win.

Also benefits `bs2 eval` REPL since same lookup path.

## Cost

~30 lines. Touches features/eval/mod.av (Runtime type, define_function, lookup_function). All eval consumers (features/comptime, bs2 eval) get the speedup automatically.

## Acceptance

- Existing eval REPL + comptime tests pass byte-identical output
- Benchmark before/after on a 50-fn eval workload
- Selfhost holds

Discovered: 2026-05-09 in vez6.2 cleanup. Generalizes the comptime-side hashmap optimization (already landed in vez6.2) to the underlying eval runtime.

title: comptime/rewrite: change-tracking walker to skip rebuilds of unchanged subtrees
description:
comptime/rewrite.av's structural walker rebuilds every Stmt/Expr node it visits, even when no descendant fold actually changed anything. For a 100k-line program with 5 comptime calls, we allocate ~100k new AST nodes; the original program structure was perfectly reusable for ~99.99% of subtrees.

## The issue

Current walk_expr:
  .Binary(l, op, r) -> .Binary(rewrite_expr(l), op, rewrite_expr(r))

Always allocates a new Binary node. If rewrite_expr returns the same value as the input, we still re-build the parent.

## Approach: classic compiler "rebuild only when needed"

Change return type to `{value: Expr, changed: bool}`. Rewriters return `changed: false` when no descendant transform fired. Parents check children's flags:
- If all children unchanged: return original input untouched (no allocation)
- If any child changed: rebuild with new children, propagate changed: true upward

For a 100k-node AST with 5 changed nodes: only the path from root to each changed node allocates. ~10× reduction in allocations vs current.

## Approach details

Wrapper type:
  type Rw<T> = { value: T, changed: bool }

Each rewrite_X: T → Rw<T>. Helpers for common shapes (rebuild-if-needed) factored out.

## Cost

Substantial refactor of rewrite.av — every match arm rebuilds. ~150 lines touched. New tests: large unchanged subtrees should preserve identity (verifiable via post-walk == pre-walk equality on those subtrees, modulo Avra's lack of identity equality… so likely measure via allocation count).

## When this matters

Sparse comptime in a large AST: a few comptime calls in a 100k-line program. Becomes load-bearing once user programs grow large AND comptime is heavily used (post vez6.11 + downstream).

## Acceptance

- rewrite.av refactor (split walk into changed-tracking variant + thin wrapper)
- New benchmark: huge AST with 1 comptime call — measure post-walk allocation count
- All existing comptime tests still pass
- Selfhost holds

Discovered: 2026-05-09 in vez6.2 cleanup. Deferred as premature for current scale.

title: comptime: memoize fold results to skip repeated identical calls
description:
Cache fold results in CompTimeRegistry — when the same (fn_name, arg_signature) pair appears multiple times in a program, return the cached folded Expr instead of re-running the eval interpreter.

## When this helps

Code-generation patterns that emit similar comptime calls repeatedly. Hand-written user code rarely has the same call twice with identical literal args, but std-cli's component expansions (post vez6.11) likely will — every `command X { ... }` block expands a similar comptime pattern.

## Approach

Add to CompTimeRegistry:

  fold_cache_index: ptr,    // string key → int index
  cached_results: List<Expr>

Cache key: serialize fn_name + arg literals as a string ("add|2|3" for `add(2, 3)`). Cache value: the folded Expr.

In fold_call:
  1. Build cache key
  2. If avra_map_has_cstr(reg.fold_cache_index, key): return cached_results[avra_map_get_cstr(...)]
  3. Otherwise: run the eval, cache the result before returning

## Estimated impact

For a program with M total comptime calls and U unique (fn, args) tuples (U <= M):
- Without cache: M × eval_cost
- With cache: U × eval_cost + (M − U) × hashmap_lookup

Hashmap lookup is ~free vs. eval. So speedup ≈ M / U. For programs where U << M (heavily templated codegen), 10× or more.

## Cost

~30 lines of code. Memory grows with U (one Expr per unique fold).

## Acceptance

- New cache hit/miss test in features/comptime/tests/
- Benchmark before/after on a synthetic repeated-call program
- File: features/comptime/mod.av (new fields), features/comptime/eval.av (cache check), tests

Discovered: 2026-05-09 in vez6.2 cleanup. Deferred as premature for current scale (low U); will become load-bearing once std-cli rewrite (vez6.11) ships.

title: comptime_lookup: O(N) linear scan — switch to hashmap when seed allows
description:
comptime_lookup is a linear scan over reg.fns. For programs with M call sites and N comptime fns, that's O(M*N) total lookup work. Acceptable today (N ≈ 0-20) but will scale poorly post std-cli rewrite (vez6.11) when each declarative DSL adds a handful of comptime fns.

Plan: add a name → index hashmap to CompTimeRegistry, populated in prepare_runtime alongside the runtime build:

  type CompTimeRegistry = {
      fns: List<CompTimeFn>,
      runtime: Runtime,
      name_index: ptr,  // string → int via avra_map_*_cstr
  }

  export fn comptime_lookup(reg: CompTimeRegistry, name: string) -> CompTimeFn? {
      if avra_map_has_cstr(reg.name_index, name) == 0 { return null }
      reg.fns[avra_map_get_cstr(reg.name_index, name)]
  }

Pattern is identical to type_registry.av and module_graph.av in core/.

BLOCKER: tried this in the vez6.2 cleanup pass; seed compiler choked when I added the `ptr` field to CompTimeRegistry. Symptoms: 'unknown field <X>' / 'instruction expected to be numbered Y' depending on which struct the seed mis-resolved next. Auto-cycle didn't fix it. Likely the seed has stale field-offset assumptions for core types and breaks when struct layouts shift.

Path forward:
1. Update the seed (make update-seed) on a clean tree, then attempt this change.
2. OR: defer until after a different change forces a seed update for unrelated reasons (then ride that update).

Estimated impact when N=20: 20× speedup on the lookup hot path, ~5% overall comptime-pass speedup. When N=100: 100×, ~20% overall. So the gain scales with comptime adoption.

Discovered: 2026-05-09 during vez6.2 cleanup pass. Tracking the existing comment in features/comptime/mod.av:171.
close_reason: Landed in commit 0b02d3f0. CompTimeRegistry.name_index: ptr (string->int hashmap) populated in prepare_runtime alongside the eval Runtime. comptime_lookup + comptime_has are now O(1) via avra_map_*_cstr. Pattern matches type_registry.av and module_graph.av.

title: Extract main.av's compile pipeline to a shared helper (4-site dup)
description:
main.av's compile pipeline (parse → desugar → resolve → expand → typeck → mono → codegen) is duplicated across 4 places:

- run_test_command (test bundle), ~line 1798
- check command match arm, ~line 2312
- test single-file match arm, ~line 2390
- compile command, ~line 2530

Each repeats: parse_program_source → desugar_program → resolve_module_files → expand_components → resolve_names → run_comptime → typecheck_program → (sometimes) monomorphize → codegen.

Adding @comptime in vez6.2 made it worse (one more line per site). Future pipeline additions (Phase 4 hygiene, Phase 6 @expand attribute) will keep multiplying.

The 4 sites do diverge slightly:
- Different error rendering (bag JSON vs human-readable)
- Different stop_after points
- Different metadata emission
- Coverage path
- Per-stage timing in compile

But the COMMON BACKBONE is identical. A pipeline fn that takes a config struct (json_output, stop_after, …) and returns a final result would let each call site declare what it needs and share the rest:

  let outcome = run_pipeline(source, path, PipelineConfig {
      json: json_output,
      stop_after: stop_after,
      target_module: target_module,
      ...
  })

Implementation: extract to features/pipeline/mod.av (or top-level pipeline/). Each existing site becomes ~10 lines of config + render-result.

Cost: half-day to design + extract. Worth doing before vez6.4-6.6 add more pipeline stages.

Discovered: 2026-05-09 during vez6.2 wiring — had to add `let post_comptime = run_comptime(named.stmts); let tc_result = typecheck_program(post_comptime)` in 4 different files.

title: Generic AST visitor — extract from desugar + comptime/rewrite duplication
description:
Two AST-walking passes in the bootstrap have ~90% identical structure:

- desugar/mod.av: walk_expr (lines 321-350), desugar_stmt (101-129), desugar_expr_list (354-359), desugar_match_arms (364-372), desugar_when_arms (376-384), desugar_field_inits (388-396)
- features/comptime/rewrite.av: walk_expr, rewrite_stmt, rewrite_expr_list, rewrite_match_arms, rewrite_when_arms, rewrite_field_inits, rewrite_select_arms

They differ only in:
1. The recursive call (desugar_expr vs rewrite_expr_with_reg)
2. The per-node hook (rewrite_call dispatcher vs try_fold_call)
3. The threaded extra arg (none vs CompTimeRegistry)

This duplication will keep growing. Every future AST-rewriting pass (e.g. const-folding, dead-code elimination, unused-binding removal) will copy the same ~50 cases.

Real fix: a generic visitor with a hook fn parameter:

  type Visitor<S> = {
      hook: (Expr, S) -> Expr,
      // S = mutable state threaded through the walk
  }

  fn walk_program<S>(stmts: StmtList, v: Visitor<S>, state: S) -> StmtList { ... }

…with closures-as-values doing the per-node work. Avra has closures + generics; the missing piece is a clean home for the generic walker.

Could live in core/ast_walk.av or similar. Migration: rewrite both desugar and comptime/rewrite to use it; new passes get it for free.

Cost: ~1 day to design + write the walker, plus migration effort.
Benefit: every future AST pass is ~30 lines instead of ~200.

Discovered: 2026-05-09 during vez6.2 cleanup. The duplication was acceptable for the second pass; will become a problem at the third (likely vez6.7's component children-validation walker).

title: Resolver false-positive 'self-init' on if-expr-with-null-else
description:
The resolver rejects let-binding an if-expression whose then-branch returns a non-null value and else-branch returns null, when the expression is constructed in a particular shape:

  let new_filter = if filter != null { rewrite_expr(filter!, reg) } else { null }

Errors with:

  resolve error: cannot read variable `new_filter` in its own initializer

`new_filter` is NOT referenced in the initializer — the resolver is confused. Workaround: extract to a helper fn that takes T? and returns T?:

  fn rewrite_opt_expr(opt: Expr?, reg: CompTimeRegistry) -> Expr? {
      if opt == null { return null }
      rewrite_expr(opt!, reg)
  }

Curiously, the equivalent shape works elsewhere — desugar/mod.av uses:

  let new_guard = if guard != null { sexpr(...) } else { null }

… and resolves cleanly. The differences I can see between the two:
- desugar's branch-value is `sexpr(...)` (SExpr)
- ours was `rewrite_expr(...)` (Expr)

Both should produce a nullable union type. No reason resolver should differ.

Hit while writing features/comptime/rewrite.av (vez6.2 slice C).

Real fix: investigate why the resolver's binding-name capture differs between these two cases. Probably a corner case in the resolver's "self-init detection" pass.

Discovered: 2026-05-09 during vez6.2 slice C work.

title: Avra doesn't support 'if let' shorthand
Test runner: failure output doesn't surface which specs failed
description:
When `bs2 test` reports "1997/2040 tests passed (43 failed)", there's no easy way to find which 43 failed. The output stream contains the failures but they're scattered among 2000 PASS lines. There's no dedicated failure summary at the end.

Repro:
  ./build/bs2 test
  # see "X/Y passed (N failed)"
  # ... but where are the N? grep FAIL — and even that misses some shapes

Compare: pytest, cargo test, rspec — all print a "FAILURES:" section at the end listing each failed test by qualified name + file:line. Fundamental for triage.

Quick fix: at end of test run, before the "X/Y passed" line, print a "FAILURES:" section listing each failed test with file:line:test_name.

Adjacent: the test runner is also flaky — same source produces 43 failures one run, 0 the next. Suspect concurrent FS state or test ordering. Worth investigating once failures are visible enough to bisect.

Discovered: 2026-05-09 during vez6.2 work — pre-commit hook failed with 43 failures, fresh re-run passed clean.

title: Avra doesn't support 'mut' on fn parameters
description:
Trying to write a recursive accumulator helper with `fn walk(acc: mut List<T>) -> List<T>` produces a parse error:

  parse error: expected parameter name

The `mut` keyword is local-var-only. Workaround: thread the accumulator through return values, OR build the mut OUTSIDE the recursion and have the helper modify it indirectly via while loops.

Hit while writing features/comptime/mod.av (vez6.2 slice A) — wanted to recurse into Module bodies while pushing entries to an accumulator.

Workaround used: while-loop with mut local + manual recursion expansion.

Real fix: allow `mut` on params (means: parameter is rebindable inside the fn body, like Rust's `mut` on bindings, not the &mut borrow concept). Generic ergonomic; would unblock natural recursive-accumulator patterns.

Discovered: 2026-05-09 during vez6.2 work.

title: Components V2 Phase 13a: UAP — uniform call syntax for fn-typed struct fields
description:
When typeck sees `expr.name(args)` and there's no impl method `name` on expr's type but there IS a struct field `name` with function type, lower the call to `(expr.name)(args)`.

**Why:** generic Avra ergonomic — useful for callbacks, strategy patterns, plugins, event handlers, DI services. Not load-bearing for the cli rewrite (which uses traits + per-instance impls), but nice to have for the broader language.

**Examples this enables:**
- `type Logger = { write: (string) -> int }; log.write("hello")` (today: `(log.write)("hello")`)
- `type Sorter<T> = { compare: (T, T) -> int }; sorter.compare(a, b)`
- `type Button = { on_click: () -> void }; btn.on_click()`

**Tasks:**
- Typeck rule: when resolving `expr.name(args)`, try impl methods first; if not found, look for fn-typed field; if found, lower to (expr.name)(args)
- Disambiguation: impl methods always win over fn-fields
- Test: round-trip with both forms; verify the codegen produces the same call shape

**Independent of all other phases** — can ship anytime. Nice-to-have.

**Design doc:** docs/2026_05_08_COMPONENTS_V2_DESIGN.md §5 (Phase 13)
close_reason: UAP for fn-typed struct fields complete. typeck/mod.av check_method_call now falls back to struct field lookup when no impl method exists, returning the field's fn-return-type. Codegen already had the indirect-call dispatch; this ticket adds typecheck symmetry. 8 spec tests covering main behaviour + edge cases. All 3 cleanup tickets (13.1/2/3) closed. Same-name impl+field disambiguation tracked as P3 follow-up (vez6.13.4).

title: Typeck drops type parameter on chained field-access through generic List<T>[i]
description:
When indexing into a generic list and accessing a field on the result in a single chained expression, typeck drops the generic type parameter and ICEs.

## Repro

```avra
let list: List<TypeDeclEntry> = ...
list[0].name == "..."  // typeck currently drops the type parameter, ICEs
```

Workaround — bind to a typed `let` first:

```avra
let entry: TypeDeclEntry = list[0]
entry.name == "..."  // works
```

## Where this surfaced

A handful of test fixtures in `bootstrap/tests/emit_metadata_fixtures/`, `bootstrap/tests/per_file_metadata_fixtures/`, and `bootstrap/tests/metadata_codec_fixtures/` had to use the explicit-let workaround during the `lkze` cons-list → `List<T>` migration.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `list[0].field` typechecks without an explicit-let binding
- [ ] Existing fixtures simplified back to the chained form
- [ ] Spec test added that exercises chained field-access on a `List<T>` element
- [ ] No regressions in bs2/bs3 fixed point

title: Build perf: replace FnTypeEntry linked list with cstr_map (kkgf followup)
description:
Profiled the bootstrap self-compile (HEAD): 66s total wall, 51s in typeck (77% of compile time).

  parse=401ms desugar=3ms resolve_mods=5095ms expand=19ms
  resolve_names=4630ms typeck=51089ms monomorphize=623ms codegen=4432ms
  total=66292ms

Likely hot spot in typeck: FnTypeEntry. It's a cons-list of (name, params, ret_ty) walked on every Ident-resolves-to-fn lookup via fn_type_get. 7 call sites in typeck/mod.av; bootstrap source has ~5000 fns. Every typecheck operation that touches a fn name pays O(n) lookup. Naive estimate: ~5000 fns × ~10 lookups/fn × 5000-entry walk = 250M ops on the linked list.

Implementation:
1. Define a struct FnTypeMeta { name, params, ret_ty } and a registry struct FnTypeReg { items: List<FnTypeMeta>, index: ptr }.
2. The `index` is an avra_map_new_cstr() instance mapping name → i (index into items).
3. fn_type_get becomes O(1): map_get(index, name) → i; items[i].
4. fn_type_register adds to items, sets map[name] = items.length-1.
5. rewrite_fn_ret_tys (the one-shot rebuild) rebuilds both items and map.

Risk: avra_map_new_cstr's int-valued payload is 64-bit. We can stuff list-index there directly. The map's lifetime needs to match the TC struct's; cleanup is implicit since TC is heap-allocated and discarded after typecheck.

Expected: typeck 51s → 5s or less (10× win on the dominant phase). Total compile: 66s → ~20s.

Validation: AVRA_TIMINGS=1 before/after; assert typeck_ms drops at least 5×. Add a microbench in tests/typeck_perf_bench (1000-fn synthetic source, measure with avra_uptime_ms diffs).

Tracking parent: forge-crafting-intepreters-kkgf.
close_reason: Already done as part of the kkgf perf work. typeck/mod.av:79 — FnTypeReg = { ord: List<FnTypeMeta>, idx: ptr (cstr_map) }. fn_type_get is O(1) via avra_map_get_cstr at typeck/mod.av:121. The cons-list FnTypeEntry was retired — comments in the file explicitly note it as the predecessor.

title: Build: subdirectory auto-discovery in dir-as-module (g2eo.1 Phase D)
description:
Phase D of dir-as-module: extend the resolver's package-entry / dir-as-module path so subdirectories are auto-discovered (not just sibling .av files), eliminating the last 49 mod decls in bootstrap source.

Current state (after 186a3240):
- 37 directories migrated to flat dir-as-module
- All sibling .av auto-loaded when mod.av has no mod decls
- Package entries also auto-load siblings via the new package-entry gate

Remaining mod decls (all are SUBDIR descents the auto-load doesn't cover):
- features/mod.av: 31 mod decls (feature registry — each child is itself a dir-as-module package)
- std-avrac/src/avrac.av: 17 mod decls (top-level subdir descents — core/, diagnostics/, parse/, codegen/, …)
- std-cli/src/cli.av: 1 mod decl (mod ui — descends into ui/)

Implementation plan:

1. In resolve_dir_module_body (or a new resolve_dir_module_body_recursive):
   - After auto-loading siblings, ALSO call list_avra_module_subdirs on the dir
   - For each subdir, synthesize Stmt.Module(subdir_basename, StmtList.End)
   - Append to the body so resolve_module_files_inner picks them up via the existing `.Module(name, _)` arm

2. resolve_module_stmt currently fails when neither `${dir}${name}.av` (sibling) nor `${dir}${name}/mod.av` (subdir) exists. Extend the lookup: if `${dir}${name}/` is a directory containing `.av` files (no mod.av required), treat that as a valid module location — call resolve_dir_module_body directly.

3. Once both pieces land, `mod foo` decls in package entries can be dropped wholesale. The resolver walks the filesystem alone.

Risk: dedup. Subdir auto-discovery would synthesize Module decls that may also be declared explicitly (transition state). The existing dedup_modules pass should handle this — same name, merged body — but verify.

Once this lands the language goal "no `mod foo` declarations anywhere" is met for the bootstrap. After that, the legacy mod-decl path can deprecate then be removed.

Tracking parent: forge-crafting-intepreters-g2eo.1.
notes:
2026-05-05 (later): tried the dedup-before-qualify fix.

Change: in resolve_package_use_and_continue, run dedup_modules on resolved.stmts BEFORE qualify_uses_recursively walks them.

Result: build works for the all-decls-present case but BREAKS THE FIXED-POINT CHECK during update-seed. bs2 → bs3 byte-identity fails. Reverted.

Implication: dedup_modules ITSELF is not idempotent — running it twice (once via my new pre-qualify call, once via the existing program-outer dedup) produces different IR than running it once. That's a separate latent bug independent of Phase D.

Possible explanations:
- dedup's group-by-name walk depends on input order. After my new pre-pass, the SAME stmts are in different positions when the outer dedup runs again, so flatten_groups emits them in different relative order.
- mod_group_merge's `append_stmt_list(b, body)` reorders content depending on which body comes first.

This means the fix needs a different approach. Options:
1. Make dedup_modules idempotent (every duplicate-merge step preserves output order regardless of input order).
2. Don't add a new dedup call; instead change synthesize_subdir_module_decls to ONLY emit decls for subdirs not already in pkg_stmts.
3. Restructure so the outer dedup is the only one that runs.

Option 2 is pragmatic. Implementation: pass pkg_stmts to synthesize_subdir_module_decls, walk the explicit decls to build a name-set, skip subdirs whose name is in the set. No duplicates → no merge complexity.
close_reason: Subdirectory auto-discovery for dir-as-module landed across the bootstrap. Final state: 0 mod decls in package source code (1 in docs/gen_test.av, intentionally excluded from auto-load). Three commits: 9bbbac5e (build/ filter fix + lib-build root synth), 41737ce5 (drop avrac.av decls), 84121c65 (drop features/+cli decls), f98732f9 (drop build/ decls + flatten use paths). 2007/2007 tests passing, seed cycled, fixed-point holds.

title: Build: per-module monomorphization (defer cross-module generic invalidation)
description:
Optimisation deferred from g2eo.1 (directory-as-module) per user decision 2026-05-04.

Current plan (g2eo.1, inline bodies):
- Cross-module generic functions are INLINED from metadata into every consuming module.
- Pro: simple — works with existing codegen pipeline, no metadata-format changes for generic bodies.
- Con: edit a generic fn → every consumer's fingerprint changes → cache invalidates the world.

Target (this ticket):
- Each module monomorphizes generics PRIVATELY using metadata signatures only.
- The generic fn's BODY is not part of consumer-side fingerprints — only its SIGNATURE is.
- Edit a generic fn's body → only its own module rebuilds. Consumers' caches survive unless the signature changed.
- Trade-off: produces N copies of the same instantiation across N consumers (linker can dedup, but each .o is bigger).

Implementation sketch:
- Metadata format keeps generic SIGNATURES (already does) but ALSO keeps the body AST as a typed-IR blob keyed by the generic fn's sym_id.
- When module M imports `fn foo<T>(x: T)`, M's codegen reads the body blob from the producer's metadata, monomorphizes locally for each T it instantiates, emits the resulting non-generic fns into M's own .o.
- Fingerprint excludes the body blob — only the signature contributes.

Pre-reqs:
- g2eo.1 dir-as-module landed and stable.
- Metadata format extension (vY) for generic-body blobs.
- Codegen pipeline can ingest a serialized fn body and codegen it as if locally defined.

Why deferred:
- Inline-bodies path is materially simpler and works for the bootstrap (which has few generics to begin with).
- Cache-invalidation pain only manifests at scale (large user codebases editing widely-imported generics frequently). Bootstrap doesn't hit it.
- Better to ship dir-as-module first and add this on top once the cache invalidation is observably painful.

Estimated effort: 3-5 days once g2eo.1 is stable.
close_reason: Closing as not-blocking. P3 optimisation that becomes interesting only when generic-body churn is observably hurting cache hit rates. With g2eo's mtime-based cache shipped, the within-package case is no longer a problem (subdirs are independent via @external_unit). For the cross-package case, signature changes still surface as typeck errors — never silent miscompile — and the perf hit is bounded by how often anyone edits a generic body. Re-file when it actually bites.

comments.author: Tristan Mathias
comments.text: P3 optimisation, not a blocker. With g2eo's mtime-based cache shipped (Phase B.4), the original problem (every generic-fn-body change invalidates every consumer's fingerprint) is mitigated for within-package compiles (subdirs are independent via @external_unit). For cross-package the inline-bodies model still rebuilds consumers — the proper fix is the codegen change described here but it's days of work and the build is functional today.

title: Lang ergonomics: retire bespoke list-of-X enums in favour of List<T>
description:

This session retired the easy wins (DepList, std-cli ×7, std-json ×2, suggest/gen/diagnostics StringList variants, CompNameList, TraitMethodList, SymbolList, UseEdgeList, CaptureList, eval ×3, coverage ×6, etc) — all cleanups, no perf change, IR shrunk ~5400 lines. See commits ac754b74..91316a07 for the pattern.

Remaining list-enum cleanups all have higher blast radius (cross-file edits, test-fixture updates, or seed cycles). Each ticket here is one bounded refactor following the same recipe:
1. Replace `enum FooList { End, Node(...) }` with `List<T>` (introducing a `type Foo = {...}` struct if the Node variant carried multiple fields).
2. Convert recursive walkers/length helpers to indexed `while i < list.length` loops.
3. Convert prepend-then-reverse patterns to `.push` direct (or walk backward to preserve byte-identical output where it matters).
4. Update consumers across files, including any test fixtures that imported the enum.
5. Verify bs2/bs3 byte-identical IR + 1965/1966 tests pass (the 1 flake is the unrelated uptime-under-10s test).

NO HACKS rule: each retire deletes the enum entirely. No List<T>-as-enum-alias workarounds, no kept-for-compat shims.

Out of scope:
- Perf wins (these are pure cleanups; perf is forge-crafting-intepreters-kkgf).

title: Build: metadata synthesizer flattens sub-module structure (blocks bootstrap-as-multi-unit)
description:
metadata_synthesize.av:synthesize_unit_body emits all decls flat under a
single Module wrap. When the consumer uses nested `use a.b.c.X` paths
(as the cli does for `use @std.avrac.diagnostics.render.{render_bag_json}`),
the resolver's tree walk can't find the leaf because the synthesized body
has no `diagnostics → render` Module nesting.

Repro:
  rm -f /tmp/cli_deps.txt
  AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 AVRA_DEPS_OUT=/tmp/cli_deps.txt build/bs2 compile packages/cli/src/main.av

Result: 188 errors, first is "undefined variable `render_bag_json`".

Root cause: each FnDeclEntry's qualified name is e.g.
`@std::avrac::diagnostics::render::render_bag_json`, but local_name(qn)
strips to just the last segment. The intermediate `diagnostics::render`
path is lost. The synthesizer needs to reconstruct nested `Stmt.Module`
wrappers from the qualified name segments.

This blocks bs2 itself from consuming @std/avrac as a separately-cached
unit, which is the real bootstrap-speedup payoff for forge-crafting-intepreters-2f54.

Architectural note: this naturally belongs to forge-crafting-intepreters-g2eo
(per-module compile granularity) — once each .av file with a `mod`
boundary is its own unit, the metadata fast-path's synthesizer needs to
emit Module nesting that mirrors the producer's mod tree.

Fix sketch: in metadata_synthesize.av, group entries by their qualified
path (after stripping unit_name prefix), emit nested Module(seg) wrappers.
Trie-build over (path_segments, decl_stmt) pairs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Multi-file libs with internal cross-mod `use` fail with --module_path wrap
description:
For \`bs2 build --lib --emit_metadata\` to work on @std/avrac (the bootstrap's
own self-host case), the auto-derived --module_path='@std::avrac' wrap needs to
re-anchor every internal \`use foo.{...}\` reference under the package
qualifier. Today only the package-load path does this (see
\`qualify_uses_recursively\` in resolver.av).

## Repro

  cd packages/std-avrac
  bs2 build --lib --emit_metadata
  → resolve error: undefined variable \`tc_er\` (line 104)

The error is a real symptom: \`tc_er\` is defined in
@std/avrac/typeck/mod.av and used cross-mod via \`use typeck.{tc_er}\`.
With the --module_path wrap, that use should resolve to
\`@std::avrac::typeck::tc_er\` but it stays as \`typeck::tc_er\` and the
resolver can't find it.

## Fix direction

Apply \`qualify_uses_recursively\` to the body of a Module wrapper that came
from --module_path, the same way the package-load path does. The wrap pattern
in resolve_module_stmt should:

1. Detect the pre-populated body (already done — that's the body-non-empty
   match landed in commit 9f877f09)
2. Walk the body and rewrite every \`use foo.X\` to \`use <module_path>.foo.X\`
   (via anchor_use_path with pkg_qual = module_path)
3. Then recurse into the rewritten body

Once that's in place, \`bs2 build --lib\` on @std/avrac itself produces a
linkable .o + matching metadata.bin. Bootstrap's Makefile can then split the
build into two units (std-avrac.o + cli.o) and saves the per-edit recompile
of 36k lines.

## Why P3

Multi-unit incremental builds work end-to-end on simple producer/consumer
fixtures (see tests/multi_unit_link_fixtures, tests/metadata_fast_path_size_test).
The bootstrap's specific use case (compile @std/avrac as its own unit) just
needs this last cross-mod use-anchor wiring.
close_reason: Fixed via qualify_uses_recursively in resolve_module_stmt's pre-populated body branch. @std/avrac (bootstrap library, 30+ internal mods) now builds cleanly as a separately-cached unit with all symbols qualified @std::avrac::*. Commit 7ed7dc7f. 5 fixture probes verify. 1872/1872 tests green.

title: Build & test perf: profile and optimize the inside-the-compiler hot path (47s → much less)
description:
The cache + dep graph + parallel workers (Phases 1–3) make the BUILD smarter. They do not make the COMPILER faster. On a clean build with no cache hits, the bootstrap still spends ~47s parsing/typechecking/codegen-ing 36k lines of Avra source — that's ~1.3 ms per source line. This ticket is the deep work to bring that number down.

Why this is the LAST ticket in the epic, not the first: optimising the compiler before the cache exists means you re-pay the optimisation gain on every no-op rebuild. With the cache, no-op rebuilds drop to <1s and the compiler's intrinsic speed only matters on cold cache / first build / changed code. So we land Phase 1–4 first to harvest the cheap orchestration wins, THEN come back here for the structural work.

Scope:
1. Instrument per-phase wall time. Today only --stop-after=<phase> exists, and the times are noisy (30-70s variance per phase). Add proper phase timers in cli/main.av wrapping each pipeline stage (parse → desugar → resolve_module_files → expand → resolve_names → typecheck → monomorphize → codegen+IR write). Emit a structured one-line summary at the end of every compile.
2. Sampling profile under `samply` or Instruments. Run `samply record ./build/bs2 compile packages/cli/src/main.av` against the bootstrap source; produce a top-20 by self-time. Identify the biggest single CPU consumer.
3. Function-level rank and target the worst offender. Likely candidates based on educated guesses (validate before acting): the recursive list helpers in core/ast.av, the resolver's symbol-table traversal, the monomorphizer's instantiation matching, codegen emit_stmt dispatch. Whatever profile actually points at, attack it.
4. Pick at least three concrete optimisations and land them with measurements. Each one ships with before/after numbers (per-phase ms + total wall clock) on the bootstrap self-compile. Examples of the kind of change that fits here:
   - Replace recursive list walks (StmtList, ExprList, ParamList) with iterative traversals where the call depth dominates time at -O0. The codebase has a documented stack-overflow case at 10 entries in render_list — there is unindexed cost everywhere similar.
   - Memoise repeated work — e.g. type lookups, symbol resolutions inside hot loops.
   - Pre-size growable allocations where the final size is knowable.
   - Cache parsed module ASTs across the multiple traversal passes (parse → resolve → typeck → mono → codegen all walk the tree separately today).
5. Re-measure. The success criterion is total wall on the bootstrap self-compile dropping by at least 50% (47s → ≤24s). If we cannot hit that with three optimisations, file follow-up tickets for what we found and explain why.

Out of scope (file separately if encountered):
- Multi-process build (that's the Phase 3 worker pool ticket).
- LLVM-side optimisations (we already use llc -O2; -O0 vs -O2 is a measurement axis, not a target).
- Algorithm-level rewrites of the type checker or resolver — call those out as separate tickets if profiling shows them dominating.

Validation:
Before/after on `time make build` from a clean state, with the cache disabled or empty. Reproduce on a clean checkout, not an incremental edit. Update the timing breakdown in the conversation history (90s total → cache+orchestration savings + compiler savings).

Tickets that should land before this one starts:
- forge-crafting-intepreters-l7nk (Phase 1 cache) — so cold-build is the only remaining problem
- forge-crafting-intepreters-eh00 (dep graph) — so we know per-unit wall time
- forge-crafting-intepreters-e20h (worker pool) — so single-unit time is what's left
- forge-crafting-intepreters-yvnp (--timings HTML) — so we can see exactly where time goes per build
notes:
Honest re-measurement of kkgf annotate fast-path wins (5 clean runs each):

Pre-optimization baseline (commit 597e4ab9):     median ~78s total
Post-optimization (commits 08e314ac + 43ae032e): median ~75s total

Real improvement: ~4-5%, smaller than the single-run 78→68
measurement suggested. Single-run timings have ~30% variance from
thermal/scheduler/system-noise; need 5+ runs to get stable medians.

Attempts this iteration that didn't pan out (reverted before commit):
1. fn_type_lookup_opt fusing fn_type_has + fn_type_lookup into one
   walk. No measurable gain — Avra's nullable wrapping cost and
   the subsequent tc_check_fn_call's 4 internal walks dominate.
2. Block expression fast-path — would need annotate_expr to return
   (Expr, ValueType) so child types are pre-computed. Bare Stmt.Expr
   payloads carry no .ty field; recovering type without re-walking
   needs the architectural change.

Real path to 47s target (20+s remaining):
- FnTypeEntry linked-list lookups (4 per fn call, thousands of
  calls) appear to be the dominant cost. Switching to a
  hashmap-backed index would change M*N → M*1.
- Avra has avra_intmap_* primitives but no string-keyed map yet.
  Would need either a string-key map utility or pre-hashing fn
  names to int sym_ids.
- ~3-5 days of focused refactor on the TC type's fn registry +
  every call site that walks it.

Iteration 2026-05-04 — single-walk fn-type lookup (commit d8db2bf7):

Refactored FnTypeEntry consumers from 4-5 walks per fn-call to 1
walk via fn_type_get + FnTypeFound { found, params, ret_ty }.
tc_check_fn_call_with consumes the record directly.

Wall-time on 8 cold/warm runs of bs2 compile cli/main.av:
  64.07, 80.43, 88.78, 82.38, 74.27, 80.04, 113.55, 114.35
  Median 81s, range 64-114s — thermal-bound, not statistically
  separable from prior 75s median.

Outcome: structural cleanup is real (dropped 137 lines from the bs2
IR, eliminated 4 dead helpers), but the wall-time win is in the
noise. Suggests the FnTypeEntry walks are NOT the dominant cost as
prior session guessed — either inlined cheaply by LLVM, or other

title: Port @std/crypto.sha256 from C-extern to pure Avra (once language allows)
description:
When the language epic for sized-ints + bytes + byte-access is complete, port the body of avra_sha256_hex / avra_sha256_file from runtime.c to @std/crypto/src/crypto.av in pure Avra. The surface (sha256_hex / sha256_file functions) does not change; the externs disappear. Validates that the language additions actually unblock the use case that motivated them.

Reference implementation: runtime.c has the C version. FIPS 180-2 / RFC 6234 has the algorithm. Test vectors already exist in packages/std-crypto/tests/sha256_test.av — they should keep passing after the port.

Depends on the in-language-crypto epic completing.
notes:
Re-benchmarked post-kkgf annotate fast-path wins (commits 08e314ac + 43ae032e):

  Pre-kkgf (per original ticket notes):
    short input (43 bytes, ~10000 iters): 24.2x slower than C
    long input (~1.8KB, ~1000 iters):      8.8x slower

  Post-kkgf (today, host apple-darwin M-series):
    short input (43 bytes, 10000 iters): 110ms pure / 12ms C = 9.2x
    long input (~1.8KB, 1000 iters):    197ms pure / 30ms C = 6.6x

Improvement: ~2.6x for short inputs, ~1.3x for long. Direction is
right but we're still well above the <3x swap threshold. Won't ship
the swap yet — pure-Avra sha256 would still ~6.6x slow down the
build cache's per-file hashing (242 .av files in @std/avrac alone,
median 1.5KB/file).

Bench source: /tmp/avra_sha256_bench.av (committed to /tmp during
bench run; not tracked in repo since it's an ad-hoc measurement).

Path forward: another kkgf round (FnTypeEntry → hashmap, deeper
annotate refactor) likely needed to hit <3x. Re-bench then.

title: Build: per-module compile granularity (each .av file with `mod` boundary = one unit)
description: Refines the Phase 2 package-level graph to module-level. Each `mod` boundary gets its own fingerprint, .ll, .o, metadata.bin. Editing one feature recompiles one module + dependents, not the whole package. Requires the metadata work in tickets 10 and 11 to be solid.
notes:
Design plan (2026-05-04 review).

Where we are
- Per-PACKAGE units already work (2f54 + iinq + xtvc + 9ixv landed).
  pre_build_path_deps spawns one bs2 per path-dep (5 today), each
  produces unit.ll/unit.o/.meta.bin, fingerprint-cached.
- collect_source_files (g2eo level-1) walks resolved stmts and
  returns the unique .av files seen. extract_per_file_metadata
  produces a per-file UnitMetadata slice. Both already in
  metadata_extract.av. Used by --per_file_metadata flag.
- Module graph extractor (build_module_graph in
  features/modules/graph_build.av) walks the entry file's mod/use
  decls and produces a ModuleGraph + List<UseEdge>.

Gap to per-MODULE units (level-2)
The codegen pipeline does NOT have a "compile one .av file in
isolation" mode today. compile_program(stmts) takes the FULL
resolved program (post-resolve_module_files) and codegens
everything inside. To make each .av file a unit we need:

1. bs2 single-file compile mode. Concretely: a flag or subcommand
   that:
   a. Parses one .av file's source.
   b. Resolves names by loading every transitive dep's .meta.bin
      (NOT its source). The resolver fast-path
      (meta_fingerprint_matches_source) already does this when
      AVRA_USE_METADATA=1; today the package boundary is the
      consumer of this. We need to extend it so the consumer is a
      single source file.
   c. Type-checks this file's stmts against the metadata stubs.
   d. Codegens ONLY this file's symbols. Imports become extern
      declarations that the linker resolves later.
   e. Emits <file>.ll + <file>.meta.bin + records the fingerprint.

   The crux is (d) — codegen_program currently emits every
   reachable Function/Type/etc. We need a filter: "only emit decls
   whose SStmt.file == target_file" (modulo Module wrapping).

2. Per-module dep graph at the .av-file level. build_module_graph
   gives module-id-keyed nodes; we need a file-keyed projection:
   foo.av -> [bar.av, baz.av] (its direct .av imports). Trivial
   given the existing graph; just walk UseEdge entries and pivot
   from origin-mod to origin-file.

3. Per-module fingerprint. sha256(file content) plus the .meta.bin
   fingerprints of every transitive dep, plus compiler hash + flags.
   hdq5's fingerprint code is package-level; needs the same shape
   at module granularity.

4. Build driver. Topo-sort the file graph, fingerprint each, dispatch
   misses to the worker pool (e20h Phase 2 pool primitive already
   exists), link the resulting .o's via link_objects (k21v).

Phasing
Phase A — feasibility: prototype the single-file compile filter
   (item 1d above) on one small file, e.g. core/registry.av.
   Confirm bs2 can produce a .ll + .meta.bin for just that file
   that links + runs against the rest. If this works, the rest is
   plumbing.
Phase B — build driver: implement items 2-4. Wire pre_build_path_deps's
   pattern but at the .av-file level. This is the bulk of the work.
Phase C — UI: per-module progress bar replaces today's misleading
   per-file-resolver-loads bar. Each module-compile is one TTY-pool
   job with the existing 5gvp progress.

Risk: item 1 (single-file codegen mode) may not be a small change.
The current codegen assumes the full resolved AST with every transitive
function body inlined. Stubbing imports as `extern fn` declarations is
straightforward in principle but the typeck/codegen pipeline has many
sites that walk imported function bodies (generics monomorphization in
particular). Need to verify whether mono can work with metadata-only
imports.

Unblocked dependencies: 9ixv (closed), iinq (closed), xtvc (closed),
2f54 (closed), eh00 (closed), k21v (closed), e20h pool primitive
(landed, Phase 2 pool_run), 5gvp TTY progress (closed).

Estimated effort: 2-4 days for Phase A+B, 1 day for Phase C. Phase A
is the one that has to land first because it determines whether the
whole approach is viable without a deeper codegen rewrite.

title: Language: typed Mutex<T> / OnceCell<T> primitives for singleton state
description:
Avra forbids `mut` globals (CLAUDE.md rule 17). Real singletons (test reporter, allocator state, registries) currently use C-side storage with primitive accessors instead — pragmatic but it pushes logic into runtime.c.

Other systems languages handle this with a typed cell + concurrency story:

- **Rust**: `static FOO: Mutex<T> = Mutex::new(...)`; lock to access. `OnceLock` for lazy init. `AtomicU64` for primitives.
- **Go**: `var foo struct { mu sync.Mutex; data T }`; lock by convention.
- **Swift**: `@MainActor var foo: T` or actors.
- **OCaml**: `ref` cells with explicit `!` / `:=`.

Add a typed singleton primitive to Avra so we can move global state out of C without violating rule 17:

## Proposed shape
```avra
// Construction with explicit init.
static REPORTER: Mutex<TestReporter> = Mutex.new(TestReporter.empty())

// Access requires .lock() — typed; can't accidentally read raw.
REPORTER.lock(|r| r.record_failure(...))
// or RAII-style
let r = REPORTER.lock()
r.record_failure(...)
// (drop releases)
```

For lazy init: `OnceCell<T>` initialized on first `.get()`.

For lock-free counters: keep AtomicI64 / AtomicU64 atoms (already exist via FFI).

## Sites to clean up once this lands

- **runtime.c spec_test state** — primitive counters + failure linked list with C accessors. Currently the only reason `features/spec_test/reporter.av` (filed as part of the bundled-test diagnostics work) needs C primitives at all. Move `AvraTestFailure` linked list to an Avra `Mutex<List<TestFailure>>` and delete the C accessors.
- **codegen LAMBDA_COUNTER** — currently `avra_next_lambda_id()` in runtime.c. Could be `AtomicI64` Avra-side.
- **type_registry interner** — currently a strmap behind FFI. The strmap stays in C (hashmap impl), but the registry-state pointer could live in a typed cell.

## Why P3
The C-primitive workaround is well-understood and isolated; this is a language-level cleanup that compounds in value as more singletons appear. Worth doing when adding more runtime state would be cumbersome — not blocking current work.

## Acceptance
- `Mutex<T>` / `OnceCell<T>` primitives in @std.sync (or core).
- Spec for typed access semantics (locking, drop-releases-lock, poisoning).
- runtime.c test-reporter primitives deleted.
- features/spec_test/reporter.av owns reporter state via `Mutex<TestReporter>`.
- Existing tests still pass; no regression in capture machinery.

title: [bug] DocsArgs.want_gen lost across function boundary in actual main.av — can't repro in isolation
description:
While trying to extract parse_docs_args from main.av (1mh6 cleanup), an extracted helper `parse_docs_args() -> DocsArgs` lost the want_gen bool across the function call boundary. Inside parse_docs_args, eprintln confirmed want_gen=1 right before `return a`. After `let args = parse_docs_args()` in the caller, args.want_gen=0. Other fields (query string, want_no_cache bool, want_print bool) survived.

Behavior:
- Inside pure_flag_apply: entry has a.want_gen=1, but `updated.want_gen=0` after `match arg { "--no-cache" -> a with { want_no_cache: true } }`. So the bug fires inside the `with` codegen, despite forge-crafting-intepreters-14s7's fix to apply_overrides + copy_struct_fields.
- Reproducing in /tmp with the same struct shape + flow patterns (mut + with + struct return + while loop + if/continue) WORKS correctly. f8 stays 1 across the chain.
- Specific to bs2's main.av compilation: same pattern works elsewhere.

What I've ruled out:
- store_field on bool field (fixed in 14s7)
- match arms vs if-else: both fail in main.av, both work in repro
- Number of fields / order: my repro mirrors DocsArgs exactly

Possible causes:
- Some interaction with the docs.gen module or its imports
- RC cleanup interference at function boundary specific to this call site
- Some specific aliasing or stale-load in this exact call graph

Workaround: don't extract parse_docs_args. Keep the inline if-chain in main.av. Filed as TODO for the post-1mh6 cleanup pass.

How to repro: re-apply the parse_docs_args extraction (see git history of main.av around commits ec8af4b6/df60ed05) and run `bs2 docs --gen <name> --no-cache --print`. Compare want_gen before vs after the pure_flag_apply call.
close_reason: Resolved by seed regeneration in commit ba3bc63c. The bug was a stale-seed manifestation of forge-crafting-intepreters-14s7: bs2's own runtime was compiled by an old seed that lacked the with_expr/codegen.av store_field fix, so bs2's parse_docs_args lost want_gen across function boundaries even though user code compiled by bs2 worked correctly. After running 'make update-seed', bs2 itself uses the fixed codegen and parse_docs_args round-trips DocsArgs cleanly. parse_docs_args extraction landed in commit f3b64e2f.

title: [bug] mut + with reassignment in struct field returns loses bool fields when other fields have been set via with
close_reason: Fixed in commit 073d6a99. apply_overrides in features/with_expr/codegen.av was using ctx.store(val, gep) which writes 8 bytes regardless of field type. For i1 (bool) fields, this clobbered up to 7 adjacent bool fields packed after the modified one. Switched to ctx.store_field which casts via cast_to(val, field_ty) — truncating i64 to i1 — before the store. Regression test added at features/with_expr/tests/with_bool_field_clobber_test.av.

title: bootstrap: prefix ! on fn-call boolean return mishandled in spec then-blocks
close_reason: Fixed in commit 9fa69501. Root cause: parse_call's postfix-attachment loop allowed Tk.Bang and Tk.Question to attach across newlines (only Tk.LeftParen and Tk.LeftBracket required same-line). So 'let s = make_state()' followed on the next line by '!check_state(s, ...)' had the prefix '!' silently consumed as a postfix force-unwrap on make_state() (a no-op), erasing the negation from the AST. Now postfix !/? require current_line == prev_line. 1434/1434 spec tests pass; selfhost holds. Regression test at packages/avrac/src/features/spec_test/tests/oj0v_postfix_bang_swallow_test.av.

title: docs.gen: avra docs --gen <symbol> writes a doc-comment stub above the decl (DEFERRED — needs std-fs)

`avra docs --gen <symbol>` synthesises a /// stub at the right line in the source file, so a developer can `tab`-fill rather than remember the format.

Synthesis rules:
- For fn: one /// summary placeholder + @param per arg + @returns if non-Void
- For type: /// summary + @field per field
- For enum: /// summary + variant table
- Keep idempotent — running twice doesn't double-stub

- Sketch the AST-driven stub generator behind `avra docs --gen --print` (writes to stdout, no file edit) so the formatter is testable independently

Proposed:

Concrete impls:
- HumanRenderer (current ANSI terminal output)
- MarkdownRenderer (current --llm output, cleaned up)
- HtmlRenderer (replaces --site; emits a static directory of pages + index)
- JsonRenderer (machine-readable; consumed by IDE plugins, CI, and lang fed-back into self)

CLI:
  avra docs --format=human        # default
  avra docs --format=html --out=docs/   # replaces --site
  avra docs --format=json foo     # IDE quickfix, single symbol
  avra docs --format=markdown --search=auth   # composes with search

- --site / --site-dir kept as deprecated aliases for --format=html --out
- HtmlRenderer produces an index.html + per-symbol pages with cross-links (uses .4's resolved refs for hyperlinks if available)

Misleading parse error when reserved keyword used in field-access position
description:
Using a reserved keyword like 'bare' as an identifier in field-access position produces a confusing error:

  let bare = some_struct
  let x = bare.field
  // → parse error: expected expression

…instead of the clearer error you get when 'bare' is used at statement start:

  let bare = 5
  // → parse error: 'bare' is a reserved keyword and cannot be used yet

The latter is much more helpful. The parser should detect reserved keywords early in identifier-position parsing regardless of whether the next token is '.', '=', etc.

Discovered: 2026-05-09 during vez6.2 cleanup pass. Used 'bare' as a local var name; got confused by the error before realizing it's reserved.
